newsitem.title: USA: US Democratic Senators urge Fed leave rates alone.
newsitem.headline: US Democratic Senators urge Fed leave rates alone.

text.p: Sen. Tom Harkin and a group of Democratic senators urged in a letter to Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan Monday that interest rates be left unchanged unless there are clear signs of inflation.

"Unless specific and definite signs of inflation can be sighted, we strongly urge you (Greenspan) and the Federal Open Market Committee to resist any action that could lead to higher interest rates," the letter said.
Harkin, an Iowa Democrat, criticized Greenspan's recent characterization of stock market sentiment as "irrational exuberance," saying his comments had made interest rates rise.
The letter also said the senators were opposed to a "pre-emptive strike" against inflation.

Harkin was among a small group of Democratic senators last year that delayed Greenspan's confirmation to another term as chairman of the Federal Reserve because the senators believed the Fed was not doing enough to promote stronger economic growth.
